title: THE HIDDEN HANDOFF
narration: Most AI team dashboards hide the most important moment: who should do the work, why that route is appropriate, and who remains accountable. Captain is an open source Web M C P control room that makes the handoff visible to both the person and the browser agent.

title: ONE MISSION, FOUR ROLES
narration: This demo uses public synthetic software release data. Sol owns architecture and final judgment. Luna handles scoped implementation. Qwen is a bounded mechanical utility. Exact tools provide schemas, tests, and hashes. The person can inspect every task, risk, acceptance rule, and recommended route.

title: SEMANTIC SITE TOOLS
narration: The page registers seven structured tools through Web M C P. The agent reads the mission, inspects task T one zero two, compares all worker routes, focuses the same item in the visible interface, and stages Luna as a reversible proposal. Exact identifiers replace screen scraping and guessed click paths.

title: SHARED AGENT STATE
narration: The visible page and the agent tools use the same state and routing logic. The comparison explains why Luna fits this medium risk implementation while the other roles do not. The agent can stage the recommendation, but only the visible Human approve route control can authorize the handoff.

title: ROUTING BECOMES PROOF
narration: After the person approves the route, Captain creates packet P K T, T one zero two, Luna. The packet binds the original task, chosen worker, evidence method, acceptance criteria, public synthetic classification, and release false state into one stable handoff contract.

title: DETERMINISTIC RECEIPT
narration: The last two Web M C P tools let the agent inspect and verify the packet. Verification recomputes the canonical J S O N S H A two fifty six digest and records a passing receipt. It still cannot approve or download. The human reviews the receipt, approves the packet, and explicitly downloads the evidence envelope.

title: HUMAN AUTHORITY
narration: The activity trace preserves who did what. Agent actions inspect, focus, stage, and verify. Human actions approve the route, approve the packet, and download it. The final record says no release was executed, and the downloaded digest matches the packet shown on screen.

title: WHY WEBMCP
narration: Captain demonstrates a bounded interaction pattern, not a claim that real workers completed a release. Seven narrow site owned tools, shared state, deterministic proof, and explicit human gates make the workflow inspectable. The working app, tests, and source are ready for the public challenge submission.
